newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to expand digital wireless in 1997.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to expand digital wireless in 1997.

text.p: AT&T Corp said on Tuesday it would expand its digital wireless services to 12 new markets in 1997, including Atlanta, Chicago, Philadelphia and Detroit.

The company, which had 600,000 digital subscribers at the end of January out of its 7.1 million U.S. wireless subscribers, said two of the markets would be launched in the second quarter, 4-6 in the third quarter and the rest in the fourth.
AT&T said that the entire wireless market was expected to grow by 15-20 percent per year over the next five years.
"We expect to grow at or above the industry rate," Steve Hooper, President and Chief Executive of AT&T's wireless unit told an analysts' conference.
The company said that revenue per subscriber had fallen in 1996 to around $60 per month, 14 percent down on the year ago figure. Hooper said the decline in 1997 would be less marked.

Hooper said that it would actively persuade its users to switch from conventional cellular service to the new digital services, which offer new features, extended battery life and fewer dropped calls.
Hooper said it was much cheaper to do this within the user base than risk losing customers to rivals and then have to regain them.
The company said that its building out of wireless networks would be largely achieved on an off-balance sheet basis which would remove the associated debt and early losses from AT&T.
AT&T will instead work with partners in joint ventures in which it will have a roughly 20 percent stake. The company said talks with partners were well advanced, but did not identify them.
